rationale: This benchmark (05-eks) is a compact numeric eigensolver (~14 KB text, 30 functions) dominated by a few hot, loop-heavy kernels (Trianglelise, Jacobi, QRiterate, DivideAndSolve), so the priority is high static-analysis confusion at minimal steady-state runtime cost. SUB and IGV get strong enablement weights (low RuntimeCost/SizeCost/Risk) because instruction substitution and global-variable indirection obscure data flow across all 30 functions essentially for free. SPLIT is favored since the five large functions (683-3343 bytes) benefit from being partitioned to degrade function-level matching at negligible overhead. FLA is kept moderately high for its strong SecurityGain against control-flow recovery on the big kernels, tempered by its size/runtime cost in tight numeric loops. BCF gets the highest cost penalties (RuntimeCost 0.7, SizeCost 0.8) because its code-blowup compounds badly on an already branch-dense floating-point workload, so it should only fire on the largest functions whose features justify it. IBR and ICALL are held at moderate security weights with elevated runtime/risk penalties: indirect branches tax hot inner loops and indirect calls add dispatch overhead with modest correctness risk in this call-sparse program, so they apply selectively rather than globally.
